words.gloss: to those who steal (error for கள்ளார்க்கு)

literal: To those who steal, the state of life will fail; to those who steal [error for: do not steal], the world of gods will not fail.
translation: For those who steal, their very existence will fail them. But for those who do not steal, the celestial world of the gods will never fail.
modern: பிறர் பொருளைத் திருடுபவர்களுக்கு அவர்களின் உயிரும் உடம்பும் நிலைக்காமல் அழிந்து போகும். திருடாதவர்களுக்குத் தேவர்களது உலகம் தவறாமல் கிடைக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the ultimate fates of thieves and honest people. Note that the provided text contains typographical errors: the second 'கள்வார்க்கு' (to those who steal) should be 'கள்ளார்க்கு' (to those who do not steal), and 'உளகு' should be 'உலகு' (world). The poet warns that for those who steal, even their 'உயிர்நிலை' (the state of life, or the body that holds life) will eventually fail and perish. In contrast, for those who maintain their integrity and do not steal, the heavenly world of the gods ('புத்தேள் உலகு') will never fail to welcome them.
